metadata.case_name: KUMARA DEBANAMA v. LUI PUI WAI AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Multiple soft tissue lacerations to the hands (including deep puncture wounds and transverse wounds to thenar eminence and volar wounds)
source: Upon admission to the A&E of the United Christian Hospital (“UCH”), the plaintiff was found to have laceration wounds over both hands and puncture wounds over the right thigh. On admission to the O&T department of the same hospital, the plaintiff was found to have the following injuries:- (a) 2 deep puncture wounds at left 3rd metacarpal-phalangeal joint with haematoma (bleeding), (b) 1 cm volar wound over left index finger with tendon and neurovascular bundle intact, (c) 3 cm transverse wound over right thenar eminence with partial cut of superficial surface and (d) 2 smaller superficial laceration wounds over volar aspect of 1st web space of right hand.

According to the joint orthopaedic report dated 3 June 2014, both experts agreed that the diagnosis were multiple soft tissue lacerations. There was no tendon or neurovascular injury in the hands. They also agreed that the treatments were standard, appropriate and adequate. They opine that the plaintiff does not require further treatment or surgery.

Clinical examinations by the experts revealed full range of movement of all the fingers, multiple well healed scars and absence of muscle wasting in either of his upper limbs. He had numbness over the thenar eminence of his right hand and there was slight weakness of his left hand grip when compared to his right hand.
